title: Evidence export fixtures and staging checklist (v0.1)
content:
Summary:

This working doc collects a small set of canonical audit/evidence payload fixtures plus a practical checklist to stage SIEM export and evidence automation changes for RBAC v2 and audit schema evolution. Purpose is to provide deterministic inputs for automated integration tests, manual QA runs in staging, and a checklist for safe rollout to prod.

Guiding principles:
- Keep fixtures minimal but representative: one of each important event type, edge cases (long identifiers, nested evidence links), and a noisy/high-throughput sample.
- Ensure backwards-compatibility tests: old-vs-new consumers should be exercised.
- Make staging checks concrete and repeatable (commands + expected outputs).
- Capture privacy-safe examples: use synthetic UUIDs and anonymized principals.

Scope / Audience:
- Owners: Security & Compliance, SRE, Observability
- Consumers: SIEM connectors, external SOC integrations, internal forensic tooling, evidence automation service
- Not in scope: full archival retention policy (separate doc), SIEM vendor-specific parsers (we provide canonical examples)

Background / Motivation:
RBAC v2 introduced role-scoped grants and transient sessions. Audit schema changes (v1 -> v2 -> v3) add an evidence array and stable event_type taxonomy. Downstream SIEM connectors currently expect a flatter payload; we need to ship a staged export transformation while validating no loss of forensic linkage. This doc helps implement and verify that transformation.

Canonical fixture set (store under test-fixtures/sanity):
1) auth.session.create.minimal.json (happy path)
- event_type: "auth.session.create"
- actor: {principal_id, actor_type}
- session: {session_id, issued_at}
- evidence: []

2) auth.session.create.with_evidence.json (session created with delegated grant)
- includes evidence array with evidence_id, evidence_type, source, linked_event_ids (one or more)

3) access.grant.role.assigned.large-principals.json (RBAC v2 semantics)
- role: {role_id, role_name, version}
- subject: {principal_id, principal_type}
- grant_metadata: {scope: "org:team:read", expires_at: ISO}

4) audit.operation.execute.kv-cache.json (runtime op with kv cache linkage)
- operation payload shows model, seq_length, cost_estimate, kv_cache_hit boolean
- evidence includes pointer to storage blob (s3://redwood-evidence/...) and evidence_hash (sha256)

5) noisy-batch.sample-1000-events.json (throughput test)
- mixed types (auth.*, access.*, audit.operation.*) with compressed timestamps to simulate bursts

6) malformed/missing-fields.json (negative test)
- missing actor, invalid timestamps, unknown event_type -> should generate validation error codes documented below

Sample canonical payload (auth.session.create.with_evidence.json):
{
  "event_id": "evi-00000000-1111-2222-3333-aaaaaaaaaaaa",
  "event_type": "auth.session.create",
  "timestamp": "2026-01-18T15:22:08Z",
  "actor": {"principal_id": "user-6507d3", "actor_type": "human"},
  "session": {"session_id": "sess-9f3a", "issued_at": "2026-01-18T15:22:08Z", "duration_s": 3600},
  "evidence": [
    {"evidence_id": "ev-bridge-01", "evidence_type": "delegation", "source": "iam-service", "linked_event_ids": ["evt-aaaa-1111"]}
  ],
  "meta": {"ingest_version": "v2", "schema_version": "audit-v2"}
}

Validation expectations / rules (sanity check matrix):
- Required top-level fields: event_id, event_type, timestamp, meta.schema_version
- Prefer: actor.principal_id, actor.actor_type, and evidence[].evidence_id when present
- Timestamps: ISO-8601 UTC, no local offsets (tests to assert parser rejects non-UTC)
- Unknown fields: allowed but logged at debug level; do not fail pipeline.

Transformation mapping for SIEM export (staging-compatible):
- Flatten: extract actor.principal_id -> siem_principal_id, evidence[].evidence_id concatenated (comma) -> siem_evidence_ids
- Denormalize role grants: role.role_name -> siem_role, grant_metadata.scope -> siem_scope
- Preserve provenance: add header fields export.schema_version (audit-v2-to-siem-v1), export.timestamp
- Obfuscation: for any principal_type == "human", there must be a hashed_principal field using HMAC-SHA256 keyed by the environment KMS reference. Raw principal_id allowed only in internal staging runs.

Staging Checklist (pre-run, run, post-run):
Pre-run:
- [ ] Deploy schema validation lambda to staging (tag: schema/audit-v2-staging)
- [ ] Ensure staging KMS alias is configured for HMAC tests (alias/staging-evidence-hmac)
- [ ] Ensure SIEM sink is a sandbox cluster (siem-staging-01) with capture retention 7d
- [ ] Load canonical fixtures into test-fixtures/staging-inputs/ (see file list above)
Run:
- [ ] Kick off export pipeline with --fixtures mode: ./infra/tools/siem-export --source=staging --fixtures=test-fixtures/staging-inputs/*
- [ ] Run automated verifier (tests/siem/verifier.py) which validates: schema conformance, evidence linkage exist in evidence-store, HMAC fields present when required
- [ ] During noisy-batch run, monitor export queue lag (SQS: export-staging-queue) and producer TPS; verify no message loss
Post-run:
- [ ] Confirm SIEM sink received expected event counts by type (query examples below)
- [ ] Verify transformation logs: for any dropped field, a debug row written to export-telemetry/drop-log with reason
- [ ] Perform spot-check on evidence_probe: download evidence blob referenced in payload and assert evidence_hash matches header

Validation Queries (examples):
- SIEM: count by event_type last 24h: `index=redwood-audit | stats count by event_type` -> expected counts matching fixtures
- Export telemetry: `export.success_count`, `export.failure_count`, `export.latency_p95` (alert if failure_count > 0 for canonical fixtures)

Automated test cases (ci/siem-export):
- test_roundtrip_preserves_evidence_linkage (uses auth.session.create.with_evidence.json)
- test_denormalize_role_grants (uses access.grant.role.assigned.large-principals.json)
- test_noisy_batch_backpressure (uses noisy-batch.sample-1000-events.json) -> ensures backpressure and retry behavior
- test_malformed_event_rejection (expects validation error code 422 and non-retryable flag)

Runtime error codes (convention):
- 400: bad_payload (malformed JSON)
- 422: validation_failed (schema mismatch or missing required fields)
- 409: evidence_conflict (evidence_hash mismatch or duplicate evidence_id)
- 503: downstream_unavailable (SIEM sink or evidence-store transient failure)

RBAC v2 interoperability notes (quick):
- RBAC v2 introduces ephemeral grants (grant_metadata.expires_at). SIEM transformations should capture both grant creation and grant expiry events. Create test fixtures for `access.grant.expired` and ensure auditors can reconstruct privilege window.
- Role versions: role.version must be preserved in export to allow for rollback reconstruction.

Privacy and PII controls:
- In public/staging exports to external vendors, raw principal_id must be replaced by hashed_principal. Hashing algorithm HMAC-SHA256 with per-env key. Tests must validate hashing is applied.
- Evidence blobs may contain sensitive payloads (input prompts). For SIEM exports, only include evidence metadata (location, hash, type) not the blob content unless explicit consent and higher tier agreement in place.

Operational runbook snippets (when export fails):
- Quick restore: re-run `./infra/tools/siem-export --replay --start-event=<event_id>` for affected event_id ranges.
- If evidence_conflict: check evidence-store logs and run `scripts/evidence/resolve-duplicates.py --evidence-id <id>`

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we standardize on evidence_id prefix (`ev-` vs `evi-`)? Agreement would simplify regex-based parsers.
- How to version transform code atomically with schema changes? (proposal: tag transforms as transform/audit-v2-to-siem-v1 and require CI gating)
- Add fixture for cross-region replication edge case (time skew > 30s)

Next steps (near term):
- Sync with Observability on required export telemetry fields (owner: Samir, due: 2026-02-28)
- Add automated verifier into staging pipeline (owner: Arjun, due: 2026-03-05)
- Create PR with fixtures + CI tests: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pulls (owner: Maya)

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight; the goal is pragmatic staging validations rather than exhaustive coverage. Add more fixtures where you spot missing edge cases.

End of doc.
